```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.6, dpi = 96,
                      out.width = "100%")
library(ggplot2)
do.call(knitr::read_chunk, list("helpers.R"))

BLUE <- "#0072B2"; ORANGE <- "#E69F00"

gm <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x[is.finite(x) & x > 0])))

theme_bench <- function()
  theme_get() +
  theme(legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.015, 0.985),
        legend.justification = c(0, 1),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.key = element_blank())

log2_axis <- function(breaks, suffix = "", ...)
  list(transform = "log2", breaks = breaks, labels = paste0(breaks, suffix), ...)

# PEtab models by first author and year, classical problems marked with a dagger
label <- function(problem) {
  classic <- c(VanDerPol_mu1000 = "van der Pol", OREGO = "OREGO", Robertson = "Robertson",
               E5 = "E5", HIRES = "HIRES", Pollution = "Pollution",
               Brusselator1D_N24 = "Brusselator, N = 24", Brusselator1D_N64 = "Brusselator, N = 64",
               FitzHughNagumo_N24 = "FitzHugh-Nagumo, N = 24",
               FitzHughNagumo_N64 = "FitzHugh-Nagumo, N = 64")
  out <- sub("^([A-Za-z]+)_.*?([0-9]{4})$", "\\1 \\2", problem, perl = TRUE)
  out <- sub("^Brannmark", "Brännmark", sub("^Raimundez", "Raimúndez",
             sub("^SalazarCavazos", "Salazar-Cavazos", out)))
  hit <- problem %in% names(classic)
  out[hit] <- paste0(classic[problem[hit]], "†")
  out
}

d <- read.csv("bench/results.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ok   <- d[d$ok, ]
auto <- ok[ok$pinned == "auto", ]

# plain solves per problem, backend and tolerance: the unit of the derivative costs
plain <- auto[auto$mode == "nosens", c("problem", "backend", "rtol", "time_ms")]
names(plain)[4] <- "t_plain"
```

The integrators of `cppODE()` and `cvode()` (SUNDIALS CVODES) on $43$
problems. Both take right-hand side, Jacobian, events and linear solver
from one expression graph; only the numerical cores differ. Results come from one saved run in
`vignettes/articles/bench/`; the suite is in
[`benchmarks/`](https://github.com/dModverse/cppDE/tree/master/benchmarks).

## Benchmark setup

- **Problems:** $33$ models of the PEtab benchmark collection
  [@hass2019benchmark; @schmiester2021petab] and $10$ classical test
  problems, $n_x = 2$ to $504$.
- **Derivatives:** forward sensitivities in up to $M = 32$ parameters,
  reverse on Lang and Chen ($M \ge 120$); `cppODE()` by forward automatic
  differentiation, `cvode()` by the CVODES sensitivity equations.
- **Solver:** BDF/NDF, automatic linear solver, at
  $(\mathrm{rtol}, \mathrm{atol}) \in \{(10^{-4}, 10^{-6}),
  (10^{-7}, 10^{-9}), (10^{-10}, 10^{-12})\}$; shared output grid and
  initial values; no R calls during the solve.
- **Timing:** median of five batches of at least $0.25$ s, both backends
  of a cell in one worker, AMD EPYC 7513 nodes with twelve workers;
  ratios are geometric means over the tolerances.
- **PEtab import:** from SBML; a switch in time inside the simulated
  window becomes a time-triggered event with an undifferentiated
  switching time. Differentiated are the estimated parameters entering
  the ODE, initial values only if estimated. Trajectories start from the
  SBML initial values, without pre-equilibration.

```{r style, include = FALSE}
```

```{r problems}
pr <- unique(auto[auto$backend == "cppde" & auto$mode == "sens1",
                  c("problem", "nstates", "nsens")])
pr <- pr[order(pr$nstates, tolower(pr$problem)), ]
tab <- data.frame(problem = label(pr$problem), nx = pr$nstates, M = pr$nsens)
blocks <- split(tab, rep(1:3, each = ceiling(nrow(tab) / 3))[seq_len(nrow(tab))])
blocks <- lapply(blocks, function(b) b[seq_len(max(sapply(blocks, nrow))), ])
wide <- do.call(cbind, unname(blocks))
wide[is.na(wide)] <- ""
names(wide) <- rep(c("problem", "$n_x$", "$M$"), 3)
knitr::kable(wide, row.names = FALSE, align = rep(c("l", "r", "r"), 3),
             caption = paste("Benchmark problems with their numbers of states $n_x$ and",
                             "differentiated parameters $M$. PEtab models are named by first",
                             "author and year; † marks the classical test problems, van der",
                             "Pol at $\\mu = 1000$ and the one-dimensional Brusselator and",
                             "FitzHugh-Nagumo systems on $N$ grid points."))
```

## Comparison with CVODES

```{r speedup, fig.cap = "Head-to-head ratio of the two backends, one marker per problem and mode; above the line `cppODE()` is faster. The plain solve is placed at the $M$ of the matching sensitivity run."}
LABELS <- c(nosens = "without sensitivities", sens1 = "with sensitivities")
hh  <- auto[auto$mode %in% c("nosens", "sens1") & auto$deriv %in% c("none", "forward"), ]
key <- c("problem", "mode", "rtol", "nstates")
m   <- merge(hh[hh$backend == "cppde", c(key, "nsens", "time_ms")],
             hh[hh$backend == "cvode", c(key, "time_ms")],
             by = key, suffixes = c(".cp", ".cv"))
m$ratio <- m$time_ms.cv / m$time_ms.cp

# one point per problem and mode, the geometric mean over the tolerances
pp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(m, list(m$problem, m$mode), drop = TRUE),
  function(g) data.frame(problem = g$problem[1], mode = g$mode[1],
                         M = g$nsens[1], ratio = gm(g$ratio))))
Mof  <- setNames(pp$M[pp$mode == "sens1"], pp$problem[pp$mode == "sens1"])
pp$M <- unname(Mof[pp$problem])
pp   <- pp[is.finite(pp$M) & pp$M > 0, ]
pp$mode <- factor(pp$mode, levels = names(LABELS))

ggplot(pp, aes(M, ratio, color = mode, shape = mode)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, color = "gray30") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.9) +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32),
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.04))) +
  do.call(scale_y_continuous, log2_axis(c(0.71, 1, 1.41, 2, 2.83), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(nosens = BLUE, sens1 = ORANGE), labels = LABELS,
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(nosens = 1, sens1 = 2), labels = LABELS, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("differentiated parameters" ~ italic(M)),
       y = expression(italic(t)["cvode()"] / italic(t)["cppODE()"])) +
  theme_bench()
```

- **Plain solves:** `cppODE()` is faster on $41$ of $43$ problems, by a
  geometric mean of $1.15$ (step ratio $1.02$, right-hand-side
  evaluations $1.06$). The model functions are inlined into the stepper;
  CVODE calls them through function pointers and dispatches vector
  operations through the `N_Vector` table.
- **Forward sensitivities:** `cppODE()` is faster on $34$ of $41$
  problems, by $1.29$: $1.01$ for $M \le 3$, $1.22$ for $4 \le M \le 12$,
  $1.52$ for $13 \le M \le 32$. CVODES evaluates one Jacobian-vector
  product per parameter, `cppODE()` one dual evaluation of $f$ with all
  $M$ tangents (about one eleventh of the right-hand-side evaluations).
  The dual cost per state component does not depend on $M$; six of the
  seven slower problems have $M \le 6$, the slowest is Salazar-Cavazos
  ($n_x = 75$, $M = 6$, $0.67$).

## Gradient cost

```{r gradient, fig.cap = "Cost of one gradient by forward sensitivities in units of the plain solve of the same problem and backend, with least-squares lines."}
g <- merge(auto[auto$mode == "sens1" & auto$deriv == "forward",
                c("problem", "backend", "rtol", "nsens", "time_ms")],
           plain, by = c("problem", "backend", "rtol"))
g$cost <- g$time_ms / g$t_plain
g <- aggregate(cost ~ problem + backend + nsens, data = g, FUN = gm)
GLAB <- c(cppde = "cppODE()", cvode = "cvode()")

# the forward cost is linear in M: one least-squares line per backend
fit_line <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(GLAB), function(b) {
  f <- lm(cost ~ nsens, data = g[g$backend == b, ])
  M <- exp(seq(log(1), log(max(g$nsens)), length.out = 200))
  data.frame(backend = b, M = M, cost = predict(f, data.frame(nsens = M)))
}))

ggplot(g, aes(nsens, cost, color = backend)) +
  geom_line(data = fit_line, aes(M, cost), linewidth = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = backend), alpha = 0.9) +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32),
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.04))) +
  do.call(scale_y_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(cppde = BLUE, cvode = ORANGE), labels = GLAB,
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(cppde = 1, cvode = 2), labels = GLAB, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("differentiated parameters" ~ italic(M)),
       y = "gradient cost / plain solve") +
  theme_bench()
```

In units of a plain solve, a forward-sensitivity gradient costs
$1.8 + 0.60\,M$ with `cppODE()` and $1.2 + 0.84\,M$ with CVODES ($92$ and
$129$ at $M = 152$). The [discrete adjoint](methods-reverse.html) costs
$6.3$ on Chen and $3.6$ on Lang, independent of $M$; the
[CVODES adjoint](methods-cvode.html#asa) costs $27$ on Lang, $8.8$ to
$13.7$ times the discrete adjoint time.

```{r adjoint, fig.height = 3, fig.cap = "Time of one gradient by the CVODES adjoint over the time by the discrete adjoint, per model and tolerance; right of the line the discrete adjoint is faster."}
a  <- read.csv("bench/adjoint.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
a  <- a[a$ok, ]
aw <- merge(a[a$backend == "cppde", c("problem", "rtol", "nsens", "nstates", "time_ms")],
            a[a$backend == "cvode", c("problem", "rtol", "time_ms")],
            by = c("problem", "rtol"), suffixes = c(".cp", ".cv"))
aw$ratio <- aw$time_ms.cv / aw$time_ms.cp
lab <- unique(a[a$backend == "cppde" & a$problem %in% aw$problem,
                c("problem", "nsens", "nstates")])
lab$label <- sprintf("%s  (M = %d, n = %d)", sub(" [0-9]{4}$", "", label(lab$problem)),
                     lab$nsens, lab$nstates)
lab <- lab[order(lab$nsens), ]
aw$label <- factor(lab$label[match(aw$problem, lab$problem)], levels = lab$label)
aw$rtol  <- factor(format(aw$rtol, scientific = TRUE),
                   levels = format(sort(unique(aw$rtol), decreasing = TRUE),
                                   scientific = TRUE))
RCOL <- setNames(c("#9ec5f3", "#2a78d6", "#0d3b73"), levels(aw$rtol))

ggplot(aw, aes(ratio, label, color = rtol, shape = rtol)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, color = "gray30") +
  geom_point() +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = RCOL, name = "rtol") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 2, 0), name = "rtol") +
  labs(x = expression(italic(t)["CVODES adjoint"] / italic(t)["discrete adjoint"]),
       y = NULL) +
  theme_bench() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.position.inside = NULL)
```

On the six models with $M \ge 40$ (one core each), CVODES succeeds on
four, with adjoint time ratios $8.7$ to $18.8$ on Lang, Lucarelli and
Raimúndez and $1.0$ to $1.5$ on Zheng ($n_x = 15$,
about a millisecond per solve). The discrete adjoint reuses the forward
steps; CVODES chooses new backward steps and recomputes the forward state
between checkpoints. At $\mathrm{rtol} = 10^{-10}$ both
gradients deviate from the reference by $10^{-10}$ to $5 \cdot 10^{-7}$.

## Second-order derivatives

```{r hessian, fig.cap = "Cost of one Hessian of the summed outputs in units of the plain solve. The lines are power laws fitted in log-log over $M > 1$."}
h <- merge(ok[ok$mode == "sens2", c("problem", "rtol", "deriv", "nsens", "time_ms")],
           plain[plain$backend == "cppde", c("problem", "rtol", "t_plain")],
           by = c("problem", "rtol"))
h$cost <- h$time_ms / h$t_plain
h <- aggregate(cost ~ problem + deriv + nsens, data = h, FUN = gm)
HLAB <- c(`forward-forward` = "forward over forward",
          `forward-reverse` = "forward over reverse")
h$deriv <- factor(h$deriv, levels = names(HLAB))

# power laws fitted in log-log over M > 1, one per mode
pl_line <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(HLAB), function(dm) {
  s <- h[h$deriv == dm & h$nsens > 1, ]
  f <- lm(log(cost) ~ log(nsens), data = s)
  M <- exp(seq(log(1), log(max(s$nsens)), length.out = 100))
  data.frame(deriv = dm, M = M, cost = exp(predict(f, data.frame(nsens = M))),
             slope = coef(f)[2])
}))
pl_line$deriv <- factor(pl_line$deriv, levels = names(HLAB))
slopes <- tapply(pl_line$slope, pl_line$deriv, `[`, 1)
HLAB2 <- setNames(sprintf("%s, slope %.1f", HLAB, slopes[names(HLAB)]), names(HLAB))

ggplot(h, aes(nsens, cost, color = deriv)) +
  geom_line(data = pl_line, aes(M, cost), linewidth = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = deriv), alpha = 0.9) +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32),
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.04))) +
  do.call(scale_y_continuous, log2_axis(c(2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`forward-forward` = BLUE, `forward-reverse` = ORANGE),
                      labels = HLAB2, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`forward-forward` = 1, `forward-reverse` = 2),
                     labels = HLAB2, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("differentiated parameters" ~ italic(M)),
       y = "Hessian cost / plain solve") +
  theme_bench()
```

Hessian of the summed outputs, `cppODE()` only, $n_x \le 30$:
[forward over reverse](methods-forward-reverse.html) up to $32$
directions, forward over forward up to $10$ states and $10$ directions.
Cost exponents are $1.9$ (forward over forward) and $0.6$ (forward over
reverse); forward over reverse breaks even at $M = 3$ and
is $3.0$ times faster at $M = 6$, $9$ to $14$ at $M = 9, 10$. At $\mathrm{rtol} = 10^{-10}$ the
median deviation from the forward-over-forward reference Hessian is
$8.1 \cdot 10^{-10}$ (forward over forward) and $1.8 \cdot 10^{-8}$
(forward over reverse).

## Sparse linear solver

```{r sparse, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.4, out.width = "65%", fig.cap = "Gain of the sparse over the dense linear solver, one marker per model and backend."}
sw <- ok[ok$pinned != "auto" & ok$mode %in% c("nosens", "sens1") &
         ok$deriv %in% c("none", "forward"), ]
sg <- merge(sw[sw$pinned == "dense",  c("problem", "backend", "mode", "rtol", "nstates", "time_ms")],
            sw[sw$pinned == "sparse", c("problem", "backend", "mode", "rtol", "time_ms")],
            by = c("problem", "backend", "mode", "rtol"), suffixes = c(".d", ".s"))
sg$gain <- sg$time_ms.d / sg$time_ms.s
sg <- aggregate(gain ~ problem + backend + nstates, data = sg, FUN = gm)
SLAB <- c(cppde = "cppODE()", cvode = "cvode()")

ggplot(sg, aes(nstates, gain, color = backend, shape = backend)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, color = "gray30") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.9) +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512),
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  do.call(scale_y_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 1.41, 2, 2.83, 4), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(cppde = BLUE, cvode = ORANGE), labels = SLAB,
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(cppde = 1, cvode = 2), labels = SLAB, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("states" ~ italic(n)[x]),
       y = expression(italic(t)["dense"] / italic(t)["sparse"])) +
  theme_bench()
```

On seventeen models with the linear solver pinned, sparse gains $1.09$
at $n_x = 8$ to $3.3$ at $n_x = 504$ for both backends; the automatic
selection chose sparse in every case.

## Accuracy against a reference

Error: largest deviation of a state from a CVODE reference
($\mathrm{atol} = 10^{-14}$, $\mathrm{rtol} = 10^{-12}$) over the largest
reference value of the state. The median error ratio `cppODE()`/CVODE is $0.99$ without sensitivities (central $90\,\%$:
$0.51$ to $1.51$) and $1.09$ with ($0.66$ to $2.37$). The CVODE reference
favors CVODE.

::: {.wide}
```{r work-precision, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 16, fig.cap = "Work-precision of the plain solves, one panel per problem: scaled error against time per solve at the three tolerances; down and to the left is better."}
wp <- auto[auto$mode == "nosens" & is.finite(auto$err) & auto$err > 0,
           c("problem", "nstates", "backend", "rtol", "time_ms", "err")]
lev <-unique(wp[order(wp$nstates, tolower(wp$problem)), "problem"])
wp$panel <- factor(label(wp$problem), levels = label(lev))
wp <- wp[order(wp$problem, wp$backend, wp$rtol), ]

ggplot(wp, aes(time_ms, err, color = backend, shape = backend)) +
  geom_path(linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10(guide = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_log()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(cppde = BLUE, cvode = ORANGE), labels = SLAB,
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(cppde = 1, cvode = 2), labels = SLAB, name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free", ncol = 6, labeller = label_wrap_gen(18)) +
  labs(x = "time per solve [ms]", y = "scaled error") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
:::

## Failed runs

Six of $1083$ cells failed, all at $\mathrm{rtol} = 10^{-10}$: forward
sensitivities and forward over forward of `cppODE()` on Oliveira (each
linear solver) and on Weber.

## Running the suite

The suite fetches the PEtab collection once and runs in three tiers of
increasing coverage; a full run takes hours:

```sh
Rscript benchmarks/fetch-models.R
Rscript benchmarks/run-benchmarks.R --tier full --modes nosens,sens1,sens2
```

A run writes `results.csv`, a README with configuration and tables, and
the figures to `benchmarks/results/<timestamp>/`; options and cluster
runs are in the README of `benchmarks/`.
